implementation_notes: SeaORM ships keyset pagination: cake::Entity::find().cursor_by(cake::Column::Id).after(1).before(100).first(10).all(db).await? returns models strictly after a keyset position, Select::paginate(db, page_size) yields a CursorPage whose fetch_and_next() produces consecutive pages without OFFSET, and cursor_by accepts a tuple of columns for composite keys. With sqlx or diesel the classical form is hand-written - WHERE (created_at, id) < ($1, $2) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $3 plus a base64url token - and Rust's type system is no help there, only the discipline of a typed cursor struct.
pitfalls: A CursorPage is lazy: rows are fetched when it is polled, so dropping the page early truncates iteration without an error - drain it to completion or propagate a real end condition.

Cursors over a non-unique or nullable column repeat or skip rows, and composite keys must be unique as a whole; with sqlx/diesel nothing adds the tiebreaker for you, so order by the primary key or a unique index.
